reasons.boundary: The file is not in the warehouse yet, so dbt cannot see it. GX checks the file as delivered and stops a bad drop before it loads.
reasons.tolerance: A tolerance or distribution check. GX has it built in and reports the observed value; in dbt it would be a custom macro.
reasons.gx_only: No set-based SQL form of this check, so it runs in GX.
reasons.set_based: Set-based SQL on a model. It runs in the warehouse inside dbt build, moves no rows, and a failure stops downstream models.
reasons.reuse: The project already runs this exact dbt test, so the contract links to it rather than testing twice.

# Data contract: what Finance relies on for the monthly warehouse chargeback.
# Stakeholders own this file; contracts/compile.py turns each rule into a dbt test
# or a Great Expectations expectation, whichever is cheaper to run (see README.md).
contract: finance
title: Warehouse cost chargeback
version: 2.1.0
stakeholder: Finance (FP&A), monthly chargeback and budget forecast
consumer: Platform cost dashboard (dbt exposure platform_cost_and_lineage)
owner_group: platform_ops
sla:
  refreshed_by: "06:30 UTC"
  signed_off_by: "23:00 UTC"
  breach: A failed error rule stops the chargeback file going to Finance until it is fixed.

datasets:
  - name: billing_export
    kind: file
    path: seeds/platform_warehouse_metering.csv
    description: The warehouse metering export, checked as delivered and before it is loaded.
  - name: mart_cost_budget_vs_actual
    kind: model
  - name: mart_cost_by_model
    kind: model
  - name: mart_cost_daily
    kind: model

rules:
  - id: F-01
    dataset: billing_export
    check: columns_match
    columns: [warehouse_name, usage_date, credits_used_compute, credits_used_cloud_services]
    description: The export keeps the agreed column layout.
  - id: F-02
    dataset: billing_export
    check: unique_combination
    columns: [warehouse_name, usage_date]
    description: One metering row per warehouse per day, so nothing is billed twice.
  - id: F-03
    dataset: billing_export
    check: between
    column: credits_used_compute
    min: 0
    max: 5
    description: Daily compute credits are never negative or implausibly large.
  - id: F-04
    dataset: billing_export
    check: row_count
    min: 100
    max: 130
    description: A full month for four warehouses arrived, not a partial file.
  - id: F-05
    dataset: billing_export
    check: sum
    column: credits_used_compute
    min: 0
    max: 60
    description: Monthly compute stays under the 60-credit contract ceiling.
  - id: F-06
    dataset: mart_cost_budget_vs_actual
    check: unique
    column: warehouse_name
    description: Each warehouse is charged back once.
  - id: F-07
    dataset: mart_cost_budget_vs_actual
    check: accepted_values
    column: budget_status
    values: [ok, notify, forecast_over, suspended]
    description: Budget status uses the resource monitor's vocabulary.
  - id: F-08
    dataset: mart_cost_budget_vs_actual
    check: expression
    expression: "abs(cost_usd_mtd - credits_used_mtd * {{ var('credit_price_usd') }}) <= 0.01"
    description: Dollars equal credits times the contracted credit price.
  - id: F-09
    dataset: mart_cost_budget_vs_actual
    check: expression
    expression: forecast_pct_of_budget <= 100
    severity: warn
    description: No warehouse is forecast to overrun its monthly budget. A warning, not a stop.
  - id: F-10
    dataset: mart_cost_by_model
    check: reconciles
    left: sum(pct_of_dbt_cost)
    right: {value: 100}
    tolerance: 0.5
    description: Model cost shares add up to the whole dbt bill.
  - id: F-11
    dataset: mart_cost_daily
    check: accepted_values
    column: is_anomaly
    values: [false]
    mostly: 0.95
    description: At least 95% of warehouse-days burn within the normal range.

reconcile:
  - id: R-F1
    title: The billing export landed whole
    tolerance: 0.0001
    measures:
      - {label: "Billing export (file, GX)", rule: F-05}
      - {label: Loaded table, sql: "select sum(credits_used_compute) from platform_warehouse_metering"}
  - id: R-F2
    title: Reported spend equals billed spend, month to date
    tolerance: 0.01
    measures:
      - {label: Billed credits, sql: "select sum(credits_used_compute + credits_used_cloud_services) from platform_warehouse_metering where usage_date <= date '{{ var('cost_as_of_date') }}'"}
      - {label: Daily burn model, sql: "select sum(credits_used) from mart_cost_daily"}
      - {label: Budget vs actual, sql: "select sum(credits_used_mtd) from mart_cost_budget_vs_actual"}

# Data contract: what the partner scorecard promises its partners.
# Stakeholders own this file; contracts/compile.py turns each rule into a dbt test
# or a Great Expectations expectation, whichever is cheaper to run (see README.md).
contract: partners
title: Partner publishing scorecard
version: 1.3.0
stakeholder: Partner Success, on behalf of external partners
consumer: Partner release health dashboard (dbt exposure partner_release_health)
owner_group: partner_analytics
sla:

datasets:
  - name: partner_submission_feed
    kind: file
    path: seeds/raw_submissions.csv
    description: The submission feed partners send, checked as delivered and before it is loaded.
  - name: fct_submission
    kind: model
  - name: mart_partner_publishing
    kind: model

rules:
  - id: P-01
    dataset: partner_submission_feed
    check: columns_match
    columns: [submission_id, title_id, submitted_at, reviewed_at, status, build_version, return_reason]
    description: The feed keeps the agreed column layout.
  - id: P-02
    dataset: partner_submission_feed
    check: regex
    column: submission_id
    pattern: '^S\d{3}$'
    description: Submission ids follow the partner-facing format.
  - id: P-03
    dataset: partner_submission_feed
    check: accepted_values
    column: status
    values: [approved, rejected, pending]
    description: Partners only send statuses the review workflow knows.
  - id: P-04
    dataset: partner_submission_feed
    check: row_count
    min: 1
    max: 5000
    description: The daily drop is neither empty nor a runaway resend.
  - id: P-05
    dataset: partner_submission_feed
    check: between
    column: build_version
    min: 1
    max: 20
    description: Build versions are plausible resubmission counts.
  - id: P-06
    dataset: fct_submission
    check: unique
    column: submission_id
    description: Each review attempt is counted once.
  - id: P-07
    dataset: fct_submission
    check: accepted_values
    column: status
    values: [approved, rejected, pending]
    description: Every attempt carries a known review outcome.
  - id: P-08
    dataset: fct_submission
    check: expression
    expression: reviewed_at is null or reviewed_at >= submitted_at
    description: No review finishes before the build was submitted.
  - id: P-09
    dataset: fct_submission
    check: between
    column: review_hours
    max: 72
    mostly: 0.95
    description: At least 95% of reviews finish within the 72-hour review promise.
  - id: P-10
    dataset: mart_partner_publishing
    check: between
    column: first_pass_approval_pct
    min: 0
    max: 100
    description: Approval rates shown to partners are valid percentages.
  - id: P-11
    dataset: mart_partner_publishing
    check: reconciles
    left: count(*)
    right: {model: dim_partner, expression: count(*)}
    description: Every partner gets exactly one scorecard row.
  - id: P-12
    dataset: mart_partner_publishing
    check: reconciles
    left: sum(titles_submitted)
    right: {model: fct_submission, expression: count(distinct title_id)}
    description: Titles on the scorecard add up to titles actually submitted.
  - id: P-13
    dataset: mart_partner_publishing
    check: mean
    column: avg_review_hours
    min: 12
    max: 48
    description: The average review time stays inside the range partners were told to expect.

# End-of-day reconciliation: each chain must agree from the delivered file to the
# number partners see. A measure is either a rule's observed value or warehouse SQL.
reconcile:
  - id: R-P1
    title: Every submission partners sent reaches their scorecard
    tolerance: 0
    measures:
      - {label: "Partner feed (file, GX)", rule: P-04}
      - {label: Loaded table, sql: "select count(*) from raw_submissions"}
      - {label: Submission fact, sql: "select count(*) from fct_submission"}
      - {label: Partner scorecard, sql: "select sum(submission_attempts) from mart_partner_publishing"}
  - id: R-P2
    title: Published titles agree across the publishing views
    tolerance: 0
    measures:
      - {label: Storefront publications, sql: "select count(distinct title_id) from raw_publications"}
      - {label: Partner scorecard, sql: "select sum(titles_published) from mart_partner_publishing"}
      - {label: Time to shelf, sql: "select count(*) from mart_title_time_to_shelf where shelf_status = 'published'"}

files.code:
# Stakeholder data contracts

Each stakeholder owns one YAML file listing what they rely on. `partners.yml` covers
the partner scorecard and `finance.yml` the warehouse chargeback. Nobody hand-writes
the tests: a compiler turns each rule into a dbt test or a Great Expectations (GX)
expectation, depending on which is cheaper to run. At the end of the day the results
from both engines are reconciled into one verdict per stakeholder.

All data is synthetic.

## Where each rule runs

`contract_plan.py` routes every rule, checking in this order:

| Rule | Engine | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On a delivered file (partner feed, billing export) | Great Expectations | dbt can only test what is already loaded. GX checks the file as delivered, so a bad drop never loads. |
| Tolerance or distribution (`mostly`, mean, sum, row count) | Great Expectations | GX has these built in and reports the observed value. In dbt each would need a custom macro. |
| Set-based SQL on a model (unique, accepted values, ranges, expressions, cross-model totals) | dbt test | Runs in the warehouse inside `dbt build`, moves no rows, and a failure stops downstream models. |
| Same as a test the project already has | dbt (reused) | Linked to the existing test rather than run twice. |

GX on a model reads only the columns its expectations need.

## The daily run

```bash
dbt parse --profiles-dir .
python contracts/compile.py      # contracts -> tests/contracts/*.sql + contracts/gx/expectations/*.json
python contracts/validate.py --scope files   # GX on the delivered files; stops a bad drop before it loads
dbt build --profiles-dir .                   # models + every dbt test, generated contract tests included
python contracts/validate.py --scope models  # GX tolerance checks on the built models
python contracts/reconcile.py                # both engines + reconcile chains -> assets/contracts.json
```

The Airflow DAG runs the same steps. `validate_contract_files` runs before the
seed load. After the test gate, `contracts.validate_contract_models` and
`contracts.reconcile_contracts` give the daily sign-off, and publishing waits on it.

## Reconciliation

Rule results alone don't prove that the number a stakeholder sees is the number
that was delivered. Each contract therefore lists `reconcile` chains: the same
measure taken at every hop, from the delivered file (a GX observed value) through
the loaded table to the mart, which must agree within a tolerance. A contract is:

- **signed off** when every rule passes and every chain matches,
- **signed off with warnings** when only `severity: warn` rules fail,
- **held** when an error rule fails or a chain breaks. `reconcile.py` then exits
  non-zero, so CI fails and nothing publishes.

## Rule vocabulary

`unique`, `not_null`, `accepted_values` (`values`), `between` (`min`, `max`),
`regex` (`pattern`), `expression`, `reconciles` (`left`, `right`, `tolerance`),
`columns_match` and `unique_combination` (`columns`), `row_count`, `sum` and `mean`
(`min`, `max`). Any rule can take `mostly` (a share of rows that must pass) and
`severity: warn`.

"""Run the generated Great Expectations suites and record the results.

    python contracts/validate.py                 # every suite
    python contracts/validate.py --scope files   # delivered files only, before they load
    python contracts/validate.py --scope models  # models only, after the dbt build

File datasets are read as delivered (the CSV a partner or the billing system
sends). Model datasets are read from the dbt build, selecting only the columns
the suite needs. Results go to target/gx_results/<scope>.json for reconcile.py. Exits
non-zero if an error-severity expectation fails, so a bad file never loads.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys

import duckdb
import great_expectations as gx

from contract_plan import GX_SUITES, ROOT

DATABASE = ROOT / "target" / "nexus_partner_analytics.duckdb"
RESULTS = ROOT / "target" / "gx_results"
SCOPES = {"files": ("file",), "models": ("model",), "all": ("file", "model")}


def columns(suite: dict) -> list[str]:
    needed = []
    for exp in suite["expectations"]:
        kwargs = exp["kwargs"]
        for col in [kwargs.get("column"), *kwargs.get("column_list", [])]:
            if col and col not in needed:
                needed.append(col)
    return needed


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--scope", choices=SCOPES, default="all")
    kinds = SCOPES[parser.parse_args().scope]
    logging.getLogger("great_expectations").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
    context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
    context.variables.progress_bars = {"globally": False}
    files = context.data_sources.add_pandas("delivered_files")
    warehouse = context.data_sources.add_pandas("dbt_build")
    con = duckdb.connect(str(DATABASE), read_only=True) if "model" in kinds else None

    results, blocking = {kind: [] for kind in kinds}, []
    for path in sorted(GX_SUITES.glob("*.json")):
        spec = json.loads(path.read_text())
        meta = spec["meta"]
        if meta["dataset_kind"] not in kinds:
            continue
        if meta["dataset_kind"] == "file":
            asset = files.add_csv_asset(spec["name"], filepath_or_buffer=str(ROOT / meta["path"]))
            batch = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_dataframe("delivered").get_batch()
        else:
            frame = con.execute(f"select {', '.join(columns(spec))} from {meta['dataset']}").df()
            asset = warehouse.add_dataframe_asset(spec["name"])
            batch = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_dataframe("built").get_batch(batch_parameters={"dataframe": frame})
        suite = context.suites.add(gx.ExpectationSuite(**{k: v for k, v in spec.items() if k != "id"}))
        validation = batch.validate(suite)
        for item in validation.results:
            config = item.expectation_config
            result = {k: v for k, v in item.result.items() if k in (
                "observed_value", "element_count", "unexpected_count", "unexpected_percent", "partial_unexpected_list")}
            results[meta["dataset_kind"]].append({
                "rule": config.meta["rule"],
                "suite": spec["name"],
                "expectation": config.type,
                "success": bool(item.success),
                "severity": config.severity.value if hasattr(config.severity, "value") else str(config.severity),
                "result": json.loads(json.dumps(result, default=str)),
            })
            if not item.success and results[meta["dataset_kind"]][-1]["severity"] == "critical":
                blocking.append(config.meta["rule"])

    RESULTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for kind, found in results.items():
        payload = {"great_expectations_version": gx.__version__, "scope": f"{kind}s", "results": found}
        (RESULTS / f"{kind}s.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
    flat = [r for found in results.values() for r in found]
    print(f"Great Expectations: {sum(r['success'] for r in flat)} of {len(flat)} expectations met")
    if blocking:
        sys.exit("Blocking expectations failed: " + ", ".join(blocking))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
